t: You're looking at three sculptures by Veronica Ryan: a custard apple, a breadfruit and a soursop, standing on Narrow Way near St Augustine's Tower in Hackney. Hackney commissioned them as a memorial to the Windrush generation, the African-Caribbean people who came to the United Kingdom after the Second World War. They are the first permanent public sculptures in the country by a black female artist. Ryan was born in Montserrat, and her work is linked to the British Black Arts Movement. In 2022 she won the Turner Prize.
